title: Identity foundation (IAM Identity Center SSO)
hook: IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS Single Sign-On) is the enterprise identity hub. Users authenticate once via your corporate IdP and receive short-lived credentials to access multiple AWS accounts with permission sets.

blocks.text: Identity Center integrates with Okta, Azure AD, or other SAML/OIDC IdPs. Permission sets are IAM role templates assigned per account. Users see an access portal listing accounts they can enter. No long-lived IAM users. Cross-account roles are assumed via Identity Center — central audit of who accessed what account.

entries.plainDefinition: AWS SSO service for multi-account access
IAM role template for account access
User UI to pick account and role

blocks.text: Landing zones fail without identity foundation. Interviewers ask how 500 engineers access 50 accounts without 500×50 IAM users. Answer: SSO permission sets with least privilege per OU.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: corporate IdP → Identity Center → permission sets → account roles. No IAM users.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Configure IdP federation
items.body: SAML 2.0 or OIDC trust between corporate IdP and Identity Center.

items.title: Create permission sets
items.body: Map job roles: Developer, ReadOnly, SecurityAudit — least privilege.

items.title: Assign to accounts
items.body: Assign permission sets per account or OU via groups.

items.title: Audit access
items.body: CloudTrail logs sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML from Identity Center.

diagram.title: SSO flow
diagram.source:
sequenceDiagram
  User->>IdP: Login
  IdP->>IdentityCenter: SAML assertion
  User->>IdentityCenter: Pick account+role
  IdentityCenter->>Account: AssumeRole short-lived creds

snippet.label: Create permission set
snippet.explanation: Template for developer role in workload accounts.

snippet.label: Attach managed policy
snippet.explanation: Least privilege — prefer custom policy over PowerUser in prod.

snippet.label: Assign to account
snippet.code:
aws sso-admin create-account-assignment \
  --instance-arn arn:aws:sso:::instance/ssoins-abc \
  --permission-set-arn arn:aws:sso:::permissionSet/ps-abc \
  --principal-id group-dev \
  --principal-type GROUP \
  --target-id 123456789012 \
  --target-type AWS_ACCOUNT
snippet.explanation: Dev group gets DeveloperAccess in dev account only.

snippet.label: CLI login via SSO
snippet.code:
aws configure sso
aws sso login --profile prod-admin
snippet.explanation: Developers use short-lived creds — no access keys in ~/.aws/credentials.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: PowerUserAccess permission set on production accounts. IAM users alongside SSO — shadow access. No group-based assignment — manual per-user grants.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: zero IAM users with console access; permission set review quarterly; CloudTrail identity queries for break-glass usage only.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: IAM users with access keys for developers — rejected. Strong answer: Identity Center, permission sets, IdP groups, short-lived creds.

interviewTakeaways: Identity Center = corporate SSO to multi-account AWS access.
Permission sets are role templates — assign via IdP groups.
No long-lived IAM users for humans.
60s: IdP SAML to Identity Center, permission sets per role, assign groups to accounts, CloudTrail audit. Landing zone identity pillar.
Follow-up: how do CI/CD pipelines authenticate without IAM users?
commonPitfalls: IAM user access keys for humans — rejected.
Strong answer: OIDC for CI, Identity Center for humans, roles everywhere.

jsTsCorrelations.note: GitHub Actions OIDC to AWS replaces IAM user keys — same federation principle as SSO.
SSO short-lived creds like JWT expiry — design apps for token refresh not static secrets.
